criteria.criterion: Points out missing scope and decision points for different alarm types
criteria.evidence: "The runbook doesn't say which alarm this is, and the cause decides the fix." It then separates memory/disk alarms from network partitions and says: "Add a diagnosis step before any restart." It does not mention node-down as a case.

criteria.criterion: Flags simultaneous restart of all nodes/services as dangerous
criteria.evidence: Concern 1: "Restarting all three nodes at once can break the cluster... Restart one node at a time." Concern 3: "Restarting every nova and neutron service is a very large blast radius... stagger them."

criteria.criterion: Flags verification of the alarm rather than the capability
criteria.evidence: Concern 4 calls the check "too vague" and adds service-level checks: compute service list, network agent list, queue depths, consumers attached. It frames the problem as vagueness, not as checking the alarm instead of the capability. It never suggests an end-to-end test such as booting an instance.

criteria.criterion: Flags missing stop/escalation, owner and validation
criteria.evidence: It lists "A rollback or escalation path if a node doesn't rejoin" and "who can run this". It never mentions a runbook owner, a validation date or history, explicit stop conditions, or must-not-do items.

criteria.criterion: Gives findings before a rewritten version
criteria.evidence: Findings come first, but as a numbered list, not a table. No rewritten draft is given: it only offers one ("I can also draft a revised runbook"). So there is no restructured draft with decision points and TODOs.

critical_errors.evidence: The response opens with "Main concerns" and criticises every step of the runbook.

critical_errors.error: rewrites it while keeping 'restart all nodes' as an unconditional first step
critical_errors.evidence: There is no rewrite. The response asks for a diagnosis step before any restart, and for one-node-at-a-time restarts.

summary: This is a solid critique. It catches the missing alarm-type scope and decision points, and the danger of restarting all nodes and all services at once. On verification, it adds service-level checks but doesn't say the runbook checks the alarm instead of the capability. Owner, validation history and must-not-do items are missing, and only an escalation path is mentioned. It gives no findings table and no restructured draft; it only offers to write one. It commits neither critical error.
